sections.h2: What does the Macon-Bibb County government do with property tax?
sections.html:
The city of Macon and Bibb County became a single consolidated government on January 1, 2014, following a July 31, 2012 referendum that passed in both jurisdictions. A mayor elected countywide and a nine-member commission elected by district now run it, and the small city of Payne was folded in during 2015. For property owners that means a single local government, one county school district and one tax commissioner for the whole county.

The Tax Commissioner's office is at 188 Third Street, Macon, Georgia 31201, staffed on weekdays from eight to five, with a main line of (478) 621-6500 and the email address taxinfo@maconbibb.us. It mails statements, builds the annual tax digest for the state, and distributes receipts among the State of Georgia, the county government and the school board. Values come from a separate Board of Tax Assessors at (478) 621-6701.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, payments, liens, tax sales, excess funds claims.
  • Tax Assessors: values, returns, homestead applications, appeal filings.
  • Solid Waste Department: the garbage fee that appears alongside the property bill.

sections.h2: What is the Macon-Bibb housing market like for a seller?
sections.html:
Bibb is the largest county in the Macon metro area, with about 250 square miles of land along the Ocmulgee River. I-16, I-75 and I-475 cross it, and Lake Tobesofkee, west of downtown, has three county parks. Ocmulgee National Monument preserves Mississippian mound sites along the river. Every address falls in the Bibb County School District, and buses run through the Macon Transit Authority.

Bibb recorded 157,346 people in 2020 and is estimated at 157,556 as of July 2025. Tenure is almost evenly divided. The 2020 census put owners and renters at exactly 50 percent each, and the later survey shows owners at 51.4 percent. Because so many homes are rented, remember that the statement goes to the titleholder on January 1, never the tenant.

Census figures show 72,122 housing units in 2025 and 59,921 households. The median owner-occupied value is $174,500, median rent is $1,066 a month, median household income is $51,234 and 23.4 percent of residents are in poverty.

sections.h2: When are Macon-Bibb property taxes billed and due?
sections.html:
Bibb mails real and personal property statements by mid-September and splits the bill in two. One half is due October 15, the other November 15. Weekend dates slide to the following business day.

The January 1 owner of record is billed first. Should the office hear about a transfer during the 90 days before a due date, it verifies the change and bills the new owner. Lenders get a data file of amounts due, while the paper statement goes to the owner. Even with escrow, the owner remains the person responsible if a payment is missed.

Mobile homes run on their own track: statements by January 30, payment by April 1, and a decal issued once tax is paid. A late mobile home account carries the state penalty, 10 percent of the tax or $5 if that is more, along with monthly interest.

sections.h2: Can I pay late or in pieces in Macon-Bibb County?
sections.html:
• Partial payments are accepted, and interest and penalties keep accruing on the rest.
  • Mail payments need a USPS date stamp to count as on time.
  • Delinquent accounts are best paid in person once a levy has begun.

The commissioner takes partial payments, as many as you like, though whatever stays unpaid keeps gathering penalties and interest. A mailed payment is on time if it bears a USPS date stamp, and a postage meter date does not qualify. On delinquent accounts the office urges delivering payment by hand, particularly after a levy and sale notice have started.

A FiFa lien is preceded by a notice of intent, mailed to the owner with 30 days to pay in full. The lien itself goes on the General Execution Docket kept by the Clerk of Superior Court, and the office says it can be recorded when a balance stays open past 90 days. Paying the tax along with fees, penalties and interest cancels it. Liens are never sold at the counter, and the office states that it does not report to credit bureaus.

The county also bills every residential premises, occupied or vacant, for garbage service through the Solid Waste Department, on a quarterly schedule. That fee serves a different purpose from the property tax, and if you appeal the value of your property the garbage fee is due in full anyway. A household below the federal poverty guidelines can request an exemption, with the application due at the Solid Waste Department by 5 p.m. each November 1.

sections.h2: How is homestead obtained in Macon-Bibb County?
sections.html:
Homestead approvals come from the Tax Assessors. Ownership and residence on January 1 are required, and paperwork received before April 1 counts for the current year. An approved owner is not asked to renew every year, yet a move or a deed change calls for a fresh application.

Exemption amounts come from state law and local acts, so the dollar figure on your bill is what matters. Ask the assessors at (478) 621-6701 what exemption your account carries and whether you qualify for any senior relief.

sections.h2: How is a Macon-Bibb County value appealed?
sections.html:
Put the appeal in writing, send it to the Board of Tax Assessors inside 45 days of the notice, and name the appeal method you want. Valid grounds include taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption. The Tax Commissioner is an independently elected office that neither supervises nor answers to the assessors, so appeal questions belong with the assessors.

Mobile home owners get a later cutoff: 45 days after the bill is mailed or April 1, whichever falls last. State guidance allows three years after payment to claim back tax that was collected in error or unlawfully.

sections.h2: What happens to a Macon-Bibb house sold for unpaid tax?
sections.html:
With a FiFa in place, the parcel can be levied on and sold. Auctions take place on the first Tuesday of months when one is scheduled, at 11 a.m. on the courthouse steps at 206 7th Street, and bidders have to attend personally. Bidding opens at the tax plus penalties and fees. The buyer receives a sheriff's tax deed rather than the land, and must pay within two hours using cash, certified funds or a money order.

A right of redemption survives the sale. For a year, the owner or any interested party can buy the tax deed back, paying the winning bid, taxes the buyer covered later, special assessments and a 20 percent premium. Only after that year can the buyer start foreclosing the right, by certified mail and notice in the newspaper for four straight weeks. A winning bid above the amount owed turns into excess funds, which the office holds, with lienholders ahead of the record owner. Paying the tax out of sale proceeds before a levy keeps a house out of that process entirely.

faqs.q: When must Macon-Bibb property tax be paid?
faqs.a: The first installment falls on October 15 and the second on November 15, after statements are mailed by September 15. Weekend dates slide to the following business day.

faqs.q: Does Macon-Bibb accept partial tax payments?
faqs.a: Yes, in as many payments as you need. Interest and penalties continue on the unpaid balance, which can eventually be subject to a lien.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline for a Macon-Bibb assessment?
faqs.a: The window is 45 days from the notice date, and the appeal is filed in writing with the Board of Tax Assessors. Appeal help is at (478) 621-6701.

faqs.q: Where do I get a copy of my Bibb County deed?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Superior Court deed room in the courthouse at 601 Mulberry Street, Macon, GA 31201, holds warranty deed copies.

faqs.q: Is a postmark accepted for Macon-Bibb tax payments?
faqs.a: Yes, a USPS-dated postmark proves a timely current-year payment, but a postage meter date does not.
